::: {#rem-count-loops}
#### Counting the steps of loops

To find the running time (@def-running-time) of an algorithm with loops:

- a loop whose body takes the same number $s$ of steps on each of $p$ passes takes $p \cdot s$ steps,
  so the steps of nested loops multiply, as in @sol-table-loops;
- parts of an algorithm that run one after the other take the sum of their steps,
  and @thm-sum-rule turns big-O bounds for the parts into a big-O bound for the sum.

Each test of a loop's guard (@def-loop-guard) and each line of setup is also a step,
but counting them too changes the count by at most a fixed multiple plus a fixed number,
which does not change a $\Theta$ bound (@def-big-theta) on a count that is at least 1.

:::
